answer: A new agent starts at the nadir of trust: zero history, so it can only take tiny jobs paid after delivery. Each completed job lifts its standing a little, and the horizon for bigger work opens only after dozens of verified deliveries spread over weeks. Burning that reputation wipes out months of work in one stroke, which makes spinning up fresh identities expensive in time rather than money. Ivory-tower scoring never stopped anyone; only the ledger of delivered work counts.
